notes: Fix: the updater could sit on an old build saying 'up to date' forever. It read a cached copy of the release feed, so the comparison was against the wrong version
The check now uses two independent channels - the build number and the version name - and takes the newest across every source. If either says an update exists, you get it
It also reads the release feed, which is not cacheable, so a cached copy of the version file can no longer hide an update
A check that fails now says why instead of quietly claiming you are up to date; an unreadable version is reported as unknown, never as current
Installing re-reads the feed first, so the checksum always describes the file actually being downloaded
Every request is cache-busted and time-boxed, so a slow network fails with a reason instead of hanging
